scope: Four language lists in the Latin sonus family, locked by their original member digests and evidence counts. Retain a small explicit set with an attested sound/sonnet relationship; remove the other associations without deleting source lemmas.

decisions.reason: English sound (auditory sense) descends through Old French son from sonus; sonnet and its plural/derivative descend through Occitan sonet. Son 'child', net/network, planet, surnames and unrelated internal strings do not belong to the same family. The source label manually_verified on a morphological candidate is not an individual etymological review.

French sonnet has the sound/song etymology. Unqualified son and sons are sense-ambiguous with possessive and other homonyms in this sense-free corpus, while the other entries mostly match surnames or incidental son strings.
Spanish sónico is the sound-related adjective. Bare son is ambiguous with the verb ser, and the list is dominated by -son surnames, names, foreign strings and unsupported matches.
Italian suono and its clipped form suon descend from sonus; sonetto follows Old Occitan sonet. The other three are unsupported surface strings.

review_scope: Family-level selection with explicit retained records, not independent human annotation of all 6,661 exclusions. Some excluded corpus forms may have a legitimate sound-related sense or be valid compounds; restoring any of them requires separate source-level and sense review.
